You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/kvm/vmx.c`**
   - Replaced calls to `wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, vmx->spec_ctrl)` with `native_wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, vmx->spec_ctrl)` to directly write the MSR (Model Specific Register) without using an indirect call.
   - Changed `rdmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, vmx->spec_ctrl)` to `vmx->spec_ctrl = native_read_msr(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL)` to read the MSR directly.
   - Updated the call to write `0` to the MSR from `wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, 0)` to `native_wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, 0)`.

2. **File: `arch/x86/kvm/svm.c`**
   - Similar to `vmx.c`, replaced `wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, svm->spec_ctrl)` with `native_wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, svm->spec_ctrl)`.
   - Changed `rdmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, svm->spec_ctrl)` to `svm->spec_ctrl = native_read_msr(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL)`.
   - Updated the call to write `0` to the MSR from `wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, 0)` to `native_wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, 0)`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in both `vmx.c` and `svm.c` are related as they both address the handling of the `MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL` register in the context of KVM (Kernel-based Virtual Machine) for x86 architecture. The changes aim to eliminate the use of indirect calls for writing to and reading from the MSR, which enhances performance and security by preventing speculative execution vulnerabilities. The updates ensure that both the VMX (Intel Virtual Machine Extensions) and SVM (AMD Secure Virtual Machine) paths utilize the same direct methods for MSR operations, maintaining consistency across the virtualization implementations.

Here is the commit message:
KVM/x86: Remove indirect MSR op calls from SPEC_CTRL
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Having a paravirt indirect call in the IBRS restore path is not a
good idea, since we are trying to protect from speculative execution
of bogus indirect branch targets.  It is also slower, so use
native_wrmsrl() on the vmentry path too.

Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Jim Mattson <jmattson@google.com>
Cc: David Woodhouse <dwmw@amazon.co.uk>
Cc: KarimAllah Ahmed <karahmed@amazon.de>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Radim Krčmář <rkrcmar@redhat.com>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: kvm@vger.kernel.org
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d28b387fb74da95d69d2615732f50cceb38e9a4d
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20180222154318.20361-2-pbonzini@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is the use of paravirtualized indirect calls in the IBRS (Indirect Branch Restricted Speculation) restore path, which poses a security risk by allowing speculative execution of potentially malicious indirect branch targets. This can lead to vulnerabilities in the handling of speculative execution, making the system susceptible to attacks that exploit these indirect calls. The patch aims to replace these indirect calls with direct calls to improve both security and performance.

Here is the patch:
 #include <asm/irq_remapping.h>
 #include <asm/mmu_context.h>
+#include <asm/microcode.h>
 #include <asm/nospec-branch.h>
 
 	 */
 	if (vmx->spec_ctrl)
-		wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, vmx->spec_ctrl);
+		native_wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, vmx->spec_ctrl);
 
 	vmx->__launched = vmx->loaded_vmcs->launched;
 	 */
 	if (!msr_write_intercepted(vcpu, MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL))
-		rdmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, vmx->spec_ctrl);
+		vmx->spec_ctrl = native_read_msr(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL);
 
 	if (vmx->spec_ctrl)
-		wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, 0);
+		native_wrmsrl(MSR_IA32_SPEC_CTRL, 0);
 
 	/* Eliminate branch target predictions from guest mode */
